note: Each vector carries the decision it defends, in the same spirit as docs/research/credential-types/test_vectors.json. A vector whose `defends` field is empty is a vector nobody can maintain, because the next reader cannot tell an intended result from an accident. DAGs here are inline and synthetic so the suite is hermetic; test_describe.py adds separate integration checks against the real corpus.

vectors.name: constant_channel_is_suppressed
vectors.defends: Show what varies, suppress what is constant (R-ZCYM). Both nodes share an issuer, so the issuer must never appear -- it rules nothing out. This is the rule that makes the description contrastive rather than absolute, and it is the one an implementation is most likely to lose by rendering a fixed template. UPDATED for the role-first objective: `parties` is carried whenever the node has an issuer. The claim this vector defends is unaffected -- what it pins is that a channel which rules nothing out is not added FOR THAT PURPOSE, and `parties` is not there for that purpose.

vectors.name: type_is_the_head_and_always_present
vectors.defends: The head is included even when it rules nothing out, because the viewer's first question is what kind of evidence this is. Both nodes share a schema here and the type component still appears on both. UPDATED for the role-first objective: `parties` is carried whenever the node has an issuer. The claim this vector defends is unaffected -- what it pins is that a channel which rules nothing out is not added FOR THAT PURPOSE, and `parties` is not there for that purpose.

vectors.name: role_label_index_does_not_discriminate
vectors.defends: An edge label names the ROLE and then falls back to a bare index when the referrer has two of them. Left whole, licenceA and licenceB are unique, so the role channel alone would distinguish every node and the algorithm would stop before consulting anything meaningful -- emitting ITEM 03 with a longer name, in the channel that was meant to replace it. Found by running the algorithm, not by reasoning. Here the stems collide, so the issuee must be what separates them. UPDATED for the role-first objective: `parties` is carried whenever the node has an issuer, because who issued this to whom is part of what part it plays. Here it also does the separating that the issuee used to, since the relation carries the issuee inside it -- the point the vector defends is unchanged: the edge label's A/B index must not be what tells them apart.

vectors.name: role_label_that_differs_meaningfully_does_discriminate
vectors.defends: The counterweight to the vector above: stripping an index must not throw away a real role distinction. The live VVP dossier's labels are vetting, alloc, tnalloc and delsig, which differ in stem, so role alone should separate them and nothing further is needed. UPDATED for the role-first objective: `parties` is carried whenever the node has an issuer, because who issued this to whom is part of what part it plays.

vectors.name: indistinguishable_is_reported_not_fabricated
vectors.defends: The petition case: N endorsements of identical schema, identical role and identical issuee, differing in nothing the render can reach. The honest answer is that these are not separable, so distinguishing is false and every sibling is named. A label that looked like an answer here would be the worst failure this algorithm can have, because it would be invisible. UPDATED for the role-first objective: `parties` is carried whenever the node has an issuer, because who issued this to whom is part of what part it plays. The petition case is the proof that carrying it costs nothing here: all three endorsements share an issuer AND an issuee, so the relation is present in every label and separates none of them, and distinguishing stays false exactly as before.

vectors.name: absence_is_deferred_behind_positives
vectors.defends: 'The one with no issuee' discriminates without informing, so it is spent only when the positive channels are exhausted. Here the issuer separates them first, and the negative must not appear at all. UPDATED for the role-first objective: `parties` is carried whenever the node has an issuer, because who issued this to whom is part of what part it plays. The relation now separates these two before the bare issuer is reached, which is the better answer for the same reason the vector exists: a positive, informative component beats one that only tells them apart.

vectors.name: absence_is_used_when_nothing_else_remains_subject
vectors.defends: When every positive channel is constant, an absence is better than reporting indistinguishable, because it is true and it does separate them; the component is marked negative so a render can treat it differently from a positive claim. This vector used to exercise a missing ISSUEE, which the `parties` channel now subsumes -- it carries (issuer, issuee) as one value, so a missing issuee is a positive difference in the relation rather than a bare absence. It moves to the subject, which nothing subsumes: both nodes share a type, an issuer and an issuee, and one simply has no value in the field the schema designates as its subject.

vectors.name: unresolved_image_annotates_and_never_discriminates
vectors.defends: P-YY9V. A committed image that does not resolve WOULD be an effective discriminator -- 'the one whose photo is missing' picks out exactly one node -- and that is the trap: whether a portrait was disclosed is an accident of this presentation, not a fact about whose licence it is. So it surfaces as an annotation, which always shows and never discriminates, and the label falls through to the issuee. Node A is separable without its picture too -- its issuee differs from B's -- so that issuee is carried in the label as a text alternative and distinguishing_as_text is true. An earlier draft of this vector expected false, on the assumption that a node discriminated by its image is lost without it; the implementation was right and the expectation was wrong. UPDATED when the objective changed from minimal-distinguishing to role-first: a `parties` component is now carried whenever the node has an issuer, because who issued a credential to whom is part of what part it plays rather than a device for telling it apart. Node A also carries `subject_undetermined`: no subject field was supplied, and the party relation in its label does not settle what the credential is ABOUT, because the issuee is the subject only when the alignment is ordinary and the algorithm does not receive the alignment axis.

vectors.name: image_outranks_the_subject_but_does_not_replace_it
vectors.defends: Two claims at once, and the second was learned by running the algorithm over the finished accident bundle. FIRST, when both would discriminate the image wins, on two criteria that agree: the credential commits to the image by digest so the binding is cryptographic, while the subject field is an unmarked issuer claim that nothing identifies as the subject; and two thumbnails are separated by perception rather than by reading. SECOND, the subject rides along anyway, marked as a text alternative. A thumbnail is a modality the label cannot assume -- a text-only export, a screen reader, a tier too small for a picture -- and five of nine nodes in the accident bundle came back 'shown by its picture', each correct in the data model and each useless to a reader who cannot see the picture. The image is the discriminator; the subject is what survives when the picture cannot be drawn. UPDATED when the objective changed from minimal-distinguishing to role-first: a `parties` component is now carried whenever the node has an issuer, because who issued a credential to whom is part of what part it plays rather than a device for telling it apart.

vectors.name: subject_undetermined_is_announced
vectors.defends: credential-categories.md measured that field presence tells you what a credential carries, not what it is for, and that nothing in a JSON Schema expresses dominance. The algorithm does not guess a subject field from a name. When two nodes share a schema and no subject field was supplied, that gap is annotated rather than silently absorbed, so the unsolved problem stays visible in the output.

vectors.name: type_name_absent_does_not_remove_the_component
vectors.defends: Zero schemas resolve in arcviz's corpus, so the type is an opaque key: the algorithm can say two nodes are the same type and cannot say what type. The component stays, carrying name null, because a render that prints 'unknown type' tells the truth where one that omits the component does not. UPDATED when the objective changed from minimal-distinguishing to role-first: a `parties` component is now carried whenever the node has an issuer, because who issued a credential to whom is part of what part it plays rather than a device for telling it apart.

vectors.name: dates_band_into_pre_existing_and_assembled
vectors.defends: F-NR1G. A bare timestamp discriminates but says little; what carried meaning in the live VVP dossier is that two credentials sat months before the rest while three sat within a minute of each other. So the channel is the CLUSTER, and the last cluster is the assembly. Two licences years old against two statements from this week must band apart.

vectors.name: a_single_node_dag_needs_no_discriminator
vectors.defends: A presentation of one credential has no distractors, so nothing is added for the sake of telling it apart -- no date, no issuer used as a tiebreaker. What it DOES carry is its type and its party relation, because both say what the thing is rather than which one it is. An earlier version of this vector expected the type alone, written while the objective was minimality; under a role-first objective 'issued by X to Y' is not noise, it is half the content of a lone credential.

vectors.name: text_only_distinguishability_is_reported_separately
vectors.defends: P-E3Q4, pinned rather than trusted. Two nodes whose pictures differ but whose every text channel is identical are separable when the thumbnails are shown and not separable otherwise. `distinguishing` says yes and `distinguishing_as_text` says no, and a render that cannot show pictures must be able to know that without inferring it. One flag saying yes while the reader can distinguish nothing is the same class of defect as every other one this corpus exists to refuse.
